Products of tensors so far Products of tensors so far We already know some types of products related to tensors. For example, The scalar product: R × R3 → R3 given by (r, v) ↦→ rv = (rv1, rv2, rv3). The dot product: R3 × R3 → R given by (v, u) ↦→ v · u = v1u1 + v2u2 + v3u3. 2 14

# Page 6^page=6
Products of tensors so far - Part two Products of tensors so far We already know some types of products related to tensors. For example, The cross product: R3 × R3 → R given by (v, u) ↦→ v × u = (v2u3 − v3u2, −(v1u3 − v3u1), v1u2 − v2u1). The matrix products: Mat m×k(R) × Mat k×n(R) → Mat m×n(R) given by (A, B) ↦→ AB. 3 14

# Page 7^page=7
Creating new tensors from existing ones Creating new tensors from existing ones We will now explore various operations involving tensors : Addition and subtraction of tensors, Outer product, Contraction of tensors. Each of these operations provides a method to generate new tensors from existing ones. 4 14

# Page 8^page=8
Addition of tensors

# Page 9^page=9
Addition of second rank tensors Addition of second rank tensors We will now explore the sum of tensors. Let us start with the rank two case . Let Aik and Bik be the covariant components of two second-rank tensors. We can de˝ne their sum as Cik = Aik + Bik. However, we need to make sure that Cik are the components of a covariant second-rank tensor for this to make sense. Let us check whether this is the case. 5 14

# Page 10^page=10
Addition of second rank tensorsPart 2 Addition of second rank tensors We know: Aik and Bik are the components of two second-rank tensors. Thus ▶ A′ ik = L m i′ L n k′Amn, and B′ ik = L m i′ Ln k′Bmn. We need to show: ▶ C ′ ik = L m i′ L n k′Cmn. We have C′ ik = A′ ik + B′ ik = L m i′ L n k′Amn + Lm i′ Ln k′Bmn = L m i′ L n k′(Amn + Bmn) = L m i′ L n k′Cmn. 6 14

# Page 11^page=11
Addition of second rank tensors - Part 3 Addition of second rank tensors Adding two covariant second-rank tensors Aik and Bik results in another covariant second-rank tensor Aik + Bik = Cik. This new tensor is called the sum of Aik and Bik. 7 14

# Page 12^page=12
Addition of second rank tensors - Part 4 Addition of second rank tensors Similarly, we can show that Adding two rank two contravariant second-rank tensors gives a contravariant second-rank tensor Aik + Bik = Cik. Adding two rank two mixed second-rank tensors gives a mixed second-rank tensor: ▶ Ai ·k + Bi ·k = C i ·k, ▶ A·k i + B·k i = C ·k i . . 8 14

# Page 13^page=13
Addition of second rank tensors - differ- ent positions Addition of second rank tensors - di˙erent positions Adding second-rank tensors of di˙erent structures (covariant, contravariant or mixed components) does not give a tensor! Example Let Aik and Aik be the components of covariant and of a contravariant tensor, respectively. Then the transformation rules are A′ ik = Lm i′ Ln k′Amn, and B′ik = Li′ mLk′ n Bmn. 9 14

# Page 14^page=14
Addition- different positions - Part 2 Addition of second rank tensors - di˙erent positions For the sum to be a tensor, we need that one of the following holds: Cik = Aik + Bik transforms according to C′ ik = L m i′ L n k′Cmn (covariant) , Cik = Aik + Bik transforms according to Cik′ = Li′ mL k′ n Cmn (contravariant) , C·k i = Aik + Bik transforms according to C·k i ′ = Lm i′ Lk′ n Cm ·n (mixed) Ci ·k = Aik + Bik transforms according to Ci ·k′ = L i′ mL n k′Cn ·m (mixed) . 10 14

# Page 15^page=15
Addition- different positions - Part 3 Addition of second rank tensors - di˙erent positions However A′ ik + B′ ik = L m i′ L n k′Amn + L i′ mL k′ n Bmn cannot be further simpli˝ed and it does not satisfy any of the four transformation rules. It follows that Aik + Bik is not a tensor. 11 14

# Page 16^page=16
Addition of arbitrary rank tensors What about tensor of arbitrary rank? Addition of arbitrary rank tensors Addition of any number of tensors of arbitrary rank is de˝ned similarly: Pijk = Aijk + Bijk + Cijk Q ijk = Dijk + Eijk R·jkℓ i = F ·jkℓ i + G·jkℓ i etc. Important! Tensors of di˙erent ranks and structures (covariant, contravariant and di˙erent types of mixed tensors) cannot be added. 12 14

# Page 17^page=17
Example  addition of second-rank tensors Example  addition of second-rank tensors Recall that rank-two tensors can be represented by matrices. Consider the following: Mij = ( 0 −2 −3 1 2 5 1 3 4 ) and Nij = ( 7 8 9 6 5 4 1 2 3 ) . By de˝nition their sum is the tensor Cij = Mij + Nij, which is a matrix whose (i, j) component is Mij + Nij. Thus, [Cij] = [Mij + Nij] = (0 −2 −3 1 2 5 1 3 4 ) + ( 7 8 9 6 5 4 1 2 3 ) = ( 7 6 6 7 7 9 2 5 7 ) . 13 14
